main_text.l: Epicurus contrá videtur judiciu veri sensib. attribuisse λέγει ἓν ὁ
Ἐπίκουρος, ληπτὴ τὰ ἀληθέα ἕνια αὐδύσεις, ἡ προλήψεις, ἡ τὰ πάθη: ait siquidem Epicurus
judicia veritatis esse sensus, & anticipationes,
& affectiones. At Aristoteles utrūq; & sensus &
intellectus judiciū cōplexus est, intellectumq;
sensui longissimé præposuit: Nā tametsi notio-
nes intellectus deducit á sensibus & sensiliū in-
ductione rerū, & animadversione atq; experien-
tia, ut colligit: statuit tn intellectu judiciū ratio-
ne visis reb. adjūcta, sensu certius: quantoq; re-
motiō á sensu notionis genus est, tátó αἰτιωτέρον, ἀρχικώτερον, ἐπιστημονικώτερον,
καὶ τῇ φύσει πρότερον, καὶ γνωριμώτερον: causse & principio & scientiæ vici-
nius, & naturâ prius ac notius: ut jam dictū est,
sic sane notionum earum judicium præstanti-
us & excellentius.
Cap. III. De Enuntiato simplici.
ENuntiatum, est simplex aut cōposi-
tum. Simplex, est quo sententia sim-
plex enuntiatur: itaq; vno verbo conti-
netur, quo affirmato affirmatur, negato
negatur: ut, ignis urit, ignis est calidus,
ignis non est aqua: hic (ignis) est ante-
cedens: (urit) consequens. Atq; hic pri-
ma est inventarū rerum dispositio, caus-
sæ cum effecto, ut in primo exemplo:
subjecti cum adjuncto, ut in secundo:
dissentanei cū dissentaneo, ut in tertio:
quomodo argumentū quodlibet enun
tiari

page.notes: Marginal numerals 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 are line numbers; 5 and 5 (second) are shown above as printed "5" and "5I"; the printed margin numerals are reproduced as they appear. Greek passages are transcribed approximately from a small, damaged scan and may contain errors. Some words are doubtful: "tn" for "tamen"/"tñ" and "sensiliū" may be misprints; catchword "tiari" at the foot of the column is a running continuation of the word "enuntiatur".
